chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A group of people came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'Peace be upon you, O our Lord.' He asked them to repent, but they did not repent. So he dug a pit for them and ignited a fire in it, and dug another pit beside it, and connected the space between them. When they did not repent, he cast them into the pit and ignited fire in the other pit until they died.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.يَا رَبَّنَا: O our Lord (divine title used by the group)

ai.seo_question: What was the penalty for apostasy in the time of Imam Ali according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the judicial authority of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) in applying the hadd penalty for unrepentent apostates (al-Murtadd) who persist in their deviation despite warnings. The specific method of casting them into a fire-pit (Hafir) until death reflects the classical Shia juristic view of execution by fire as a distinct punitive measure for those who reject Islam after accepting it, emphasizing the gravity of the crime. This incident serves as a primary textual basis for the ruling that apostasy is punishable by death if the individual does not repent within the prescribed period.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A group of people came to Amir Al-Momineen, so they said, ‘Peace be upon you<sup>asws</sup>, ‘السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا رَبَّنَا’ O our Lord! So he told them to repent, but they did not repent. So he<sup>asws</sup> dug out a pit for them and ignited a fire in it, and dug out another pit to its side, and bore a hole between these two. So when they did not repent, he<sup>asws</sup> cast them into the pit, and ignited fire in the other pit, until they died’.
